targetWords.definition: To admonish someone is to tell them you disapprove of their behavior.
targetWords.example: The teacher admonished Mark because he was chewing gum in class.

targetWords.definition: If something is audible, then it is able to be heard.
targetWords.example: The sound of the drums was audible from miles away.

targetWords.definition: If something or someone is awesome, they are impressive or frightening.
targetWords.example: The huge military plane was an awesome sight.

targetWords.definition: To beware means to be careful of something or someone that is dangerous.
targetWords.example: You should beware of driving fast on wet roads.

targetWords.definition: To brag means to talk of one's abilities or achievements in a proud way.
targetWords.example: He had strong muscles and bragged about it to the entire class.

targetWords.definition: If someone is conscious of something, then they are aware of it.
targetWords.example: The new student was conscious of the other students staring at her.

targetWords.definition: To disagree with someone means to have a different opinion from them.
targetWords.example: • The lawyers disagreed about the best way to settle the case.

targetWords.definition: To echo means that a sound repeats itself because it bounced off an object.
targetWords.example: The child yelled over the canyon, and the wall echoed the sound.

targetWords.definition: If something is eventual, it will happen at the end of a series of events.
targetWords.example: The constant training and planning led the team to an eventual victory. hint [hint] n.

targetWords.definition: -* I quietly passed on a hint to my sister about the test.
targetWords.example: I quietly passed on a hint to my sister about the test.

targetWords.definition: — Because he got lost in the forest, the man felt like an idiot.
If something is immense, it is very large.
targetWords.example: An immense amount of money was needed to buy such a large boat.

targetWords.definition: If something is indirect, then it is not the easiest or straightest way.
targetWords.example: He chose to take the most indirect route to the coast.

targetWords.definition: An option is a choice between two or more things.
targetWords.example: The children were given the option of three houses to pick from. pastime [paestaim] n.

targetWords.definition: -♦ In the US, baseball is considered the national pastime.
targetWords.example: In the US, baseball is considered the national pastime.

targetWords.definition: If something is perfect, then it is without any mistakes.
targetWords.example: She got all the questions right, so her score was perfect.

targetWords.definition: To pinpoint something means to locate it exactly.
targetWords.example: The navigation system in my car is able to pinpoint my exact location.

targetWords.definition: To switch means to change something to something else.
targetWords.example: Mom switched the TV station from the news to her favorite show.

targetWords.definition: If something or someone is thorough, then they are complete in everyway.
targetWords.example: Tina did a thorough job of cleaning the stains out of the carpet.

targetWords.definition: To torment someone means to cause them to suffer on purpose.
targetWords.example: She tormented her little brother by taking his favorite toy.

story.title: The Young Man
story.passage:
A proud young man was looking for a new pastime. He heard about people hiking in

the national parks and decided to try it for himself. As he started his stroll, an old man

walked up to him.

"Don't go this way," the old man said. "Beware. The paths are not clear. It's easy to

become lost."

But the young man disagreed with the old man and bragged that he had a perfect

understanding of the park. "I studied maps of this area," he told him. "I believe I have a

thorough knowledge of these trails. I won't become lost."

The old man listened to the young man and then admonished him for his pride.

"I have walked these trails my entire life," he said. "If you think you will be safe, then

go ahead."

The young man ignored the old man and started along the trail.

Whenever he had to choose between an easy or difficult route, he always chose the

more difficult option. In addition, he was not conscious of which direction he was going.

After a while, he decided to return home. Because his course through the wilderness was

so indirect, he had no idea where he was.

He looked at his map but could not pinpoint his location. He walked one path after

another but soon realized he was lost.

The sun was going down, and sudden strong winds gave a hint that it might rain.

Immense clouds filled the sky. Awesome sounds of thunder were audible from all

directions. It echoed off the mountains. The thought of the eventual storm tormented the

young man. He hurried in one direction, but soon switched out of confusion. Luckily, it

led him out of the park.

When he arrived home, he knew that he had acted like

an idiot. He realized he was lucky to be alive. He decided

to listen to people with more experience than himself.
